<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8c85141c5b7575f75a3fb638c11c934f49f75e42` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `75e09b02cfeb436a52936a3a5c6767caa8b6a212` — the merge of head `23b58a388b252f21dc2f7719a493da2c1198a10f` into base `8c85141c5b7575f75a3fb638c11c934f49f75e42`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 75e09b02cfeb436a52936a3a5c6767caa8b6a212 && git checkout 75e09b02cfeb436a52936a3a5c6767caa8b6a212
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8c85141c5b7575f75a3fb638c11c934f49f75e42 23b58a388b252f21dc2f7719a493da2c1198a10f && git checkout -B drift-repro 8c85141c5b7575f75a3fb638c11c934f49f75e42 && git merge --no-ff 23b58a388b252f21dc2f7719a493da2c1198a10f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8c85141c5b7575f75a3fb638c11c934f49f75e42
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8c85141c5b7575f75a3fb638c11c934f49f75e42` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `60d1a418f059bebf76472b37dd04de83697d71d4`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #23657's body and all four comments (triage 6191435680, claim 6196478876, dispatch 6196513781, os-dev-report 6197717474); PR #23706's body, file list and net diff `origin/main...60d1a418f` (6 files, +306/−14, merge base `3bc407d30`); the 39 check-runs on the head (30 success, 6 skipped, 3 still in progress: Test Core 2/6, 3/6 and 4/6; none failed. Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, TypeScript Type Check and every Type Check and Lint lane are green). Cited code read at the head: `resolveWriteHead`, `headAt`, `put`, `lockAccepts` and `delete` in `sys-metadata-repository.ts`; `packagelessDraftAddress`, `packagelessAddress`, `packagelessReadAddress`, `saveMetaItem`, `saveWriteBinding`, `authoredLockFamily`, `storedBodyForCarryForward` and `deleteMetaItem` in `protocol.ts`; `SaveMetaItemRequestSchema` and `PublishMetaItemRequestSchema` in `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`. Judged against AGENTS.md Prime Directives #10 and #12 and Post-Task step 3 (changeset level, the `Clause-②` arms, the ADR-0087 disposition), ADR-0048, ADR-0070 TL;DR 1, ADR-0086 D3, ADR-0087's pre-GA level amendment (#18003) with `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`'s header, and pm-dispatch's `contract-review.md` and `execution-duties.md` (the `Clause-②` criterion and its narrowing line).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Two or more packages' drafts, no package-unbound draft, no active row bound to a package.** The draft save naming no package went from `200` (it minted a package-unbound draft) to `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` with the `?package=` remedy, and nothing is written to `sys_metadata`. RIGHT:
   - The card's Wanted, the triage grade and the dispatch all rule option A.
   - The refusal is the existing `packagelessAddressAmbiguityRefusal('save')` branch in `put` (#23297), so the code, status and words match the publish's and the discard's.
   - It is pinned in the repository (both storage orders) and on the REST routes for all three doors.
   - For a `flow` with an explicit credential, the channel write still precedes `put`. That is the pre-existing ⚠️ in `saveMetaItem`, and the channel slot moved before this head too, so it is not introduced here.
2. **Only package Q's draft, same item.** The save updates Q's draft (receipt `package=Q`) and no longer mints a package-unbound draft beside it. RIGHT: ADR-0070 TL;DR 1, and the unbound arm keeps ADR-0048 prefer-local. Every judge that reads the head follows, because each asks `headAt`, the one resolution `put` locks on (#22128): the strict draft read's `version`, the lock parent, the credential carry-forward, the `_lock` family carry and `saveWriteBinding`. Three derived accept-set moves follow. Each is right, each pulls back to a declared contract, and none adds a key or value:
   - (a) `If-Match` with Q's draft token on a save naming none: `409 METADATA_CONFLICT` becomes accepted (#22114 token parity). Pinned on REST and named in the changeset.
   - (b) `If-None-Match: *` (a `null` parent) on a save naming none: a `200` create becomes `409 METADATA_CONFLICT`, because the #23406 first-write pin now meets Q's draft. This is a second narrowing in the one-package arm. Right, but the changeset's TO does not name it.
   - (c) A permission-set draft save naming none whose body declares `packageId` Q: `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` becomes accepted, because ADR-0086 D3 judges against the binding the write resolves. A body naming another package is still refused, and the refusal now names Q. Right, but unnamed.
   - The arm also covers an item whose only active row is package-unbound (`bindings.size === 0`). That matches the changeset's "no active row bound to one" and what `packagelessDraftAddress` already resolved.
3. **Unchanged cases.** A package-unbound draft (with or without packages' drafts beside it), an active binding, a save naming a package, and a brand-new item all behave as before. RIGHT; controls are pinned in both layers.
4. **`packagelessDraftAddress` now asks `unboundItemDraftAddress`.** Behaviour is preserved: the same four outcomes, with `into` equal to `key` as before. RIGHT; this is the shared rule H2 asked for.
5. **Draft discard receipt.** It now reads `Draft discarded (package=Q) — TYPE/NAME. [seq=N]` whenever the removed draft is bound to a package, the named discard included. A package-unbound draft's receipt is byte-identical. RIGHT (the card's same-family line). This is message text, not an accept set. Nothing in the repo parses it, and the pinned objectui sha only matches `toContain('Draft discarded')`.
6. **Public surface.** `unboundItemDraftAddress` is exported from its module but not from `src/index.ts`, and the package's `exports` map has only `.`. No published export or type moves. RIGHT.
7. **WRONG: the narrowed door's published contract text is left false.** `SaveMetaItemRequestSchema.packageId` (`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` lines 837–854) ships in `@objectstack/spec/api` and is rendered at `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx:2745`. It says a `draft` save naming no package writes the draft of the active row's package "when it is package-bound …, else the env-local draft". At this head that is false on both arms the diff changes: with only Q's draft the save writes Q's draft, and with two or more packages' drafts it is refused `409`. PR #23654 amended the publish's and the discard's `packageId` descriptions for this same rule (`'@objectstack/spec': patch`). After this head, the three doors' runtime agrees but their published descriptions do not, so the disagreement this card closes moves into the contract. This falls under Prime Directive #10 (declared ≠ enforced) and #12 (the spec is the one contract; change it deliberately).

### ② Semver level

- `'@objectstack/metadata-protocol': minor` with the **BREAKING** banner and `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is RIGHT for an accept-set narrowing while `.changeset/pre.json` is in pre mode. ADR-0087 (#18003): before GA a break ships `minor`, and the banner plus the disposition carry the breaking-ness. The pending narrowings are graded the same way (for example 23495 and 23462).
- The disposition's facts hold. No spec key, export or stored shape moves, no stored row is rewritten, and the remedy is the request's `?package=`.
- Only metadata-protocol's `dist` moves; `rest` changes a test file outside its `files`. Check Changeset is green on the head.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` in the changeset and `Clause-②: no` in the PR body (the claim's line, verbatim) are RIGHT. A narrowing is `no` under execution-duties' narrowing line. 2(a) and 2(c) add no key or value to a published payload and pull back to declared contracts (#22114, ADR-0086 D3), so they do not make it `yes`.
- Owed once item 7 is fixed: `'@objectstack/spec': patch` beside the minor.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **OQ1** (does a door reach the two-package state?): A, answered. A `?mode=draft&package=Q` save then `&package=R` over a never-published item reaches it on the real routes; the REST pin builds it that way. The card, the triage grade and the dispatch already rule the narrowing.
- **OQ2** (shared pure rule, or the protocol passing `packageId` to `put`?): A, answered. `resolveWriteHead` feeds `put` and `headAt` alike: the lock parent, the read's `version`, the carry-forward, the `_lock` family and `saveWriteBinding`. B would fix only `saveMetaItem`'s put and leave `headAt` on the unbound key, which reopens #22128's split. The two row readers differ only in transaction scope and unprovisioned-store handling. Legacy organization rows are refused at boot (ADR-0131 D6), so both readers see the same rows.
- **OQ3** (strict draft read content over [package-unbound, Q] with no active binding): A for this PR. The head moves neither that state's `version` (still the unbound draft) nor its content selection (`packagelessReadAddress` gives any row, served as `findServedOverlayRow`'s first match). ESCALATED to the seat: the state is reachable through doors (an unbound draft first, then `?package=Q`), and serving a content row other than the version row is the #8907 coin-toss shape. It is a measure-first candidate, not a condition of this PR.
- **`[seq=0]` on the discard receipt** (out-of-scope note): by design. A draft delete writes no history event, so `eventSeq` stays 0 in `SysMetadataRepository.delete`. No card.
- **Fixture triage** in `protocol.packageless-save-address.test.ts`: right. Only setup lines change and the assertions are untouched. Both storage orders stay covered by seeding the legacy row that the now-fixed save used to mint, so this is not a repaint to green.
- **`Clause-②` spelling** (PR body vs changeset): consistent, see ②. The worktree and commit-trailer deviations are process matters with no contract effect.
- **Neighbours:** the dev reports PR #23683 and the #23514 branch merge-tree clean. PR #23418 is NOT MEASURED and stays the seat's landing-window check.
- **Raised here, not flagged by the dev:** item 7 (blocking), and 2(b) and 2(c), which the changeset's FROM/TO should name when it is next edited.

**Remedy for item 7:**
- Rewrite the draft sentence of `SaveMetaItemRequestSchema.packageId` to the head's rule. With an active binding it is unchanged. With none, the package-unbound draft, else the one package's draft, refused `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` when two or more packages hold drafts. While there, also state #23297's two-active-packages refusal.
- Regenerate with `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec gen:schema` and `gen:docs`.
- Add `'@objectstack/spec': patch`.
- That puts `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` in the file list, so the re-review is owed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on the schema face, with a `Scope:` line.

**Verified, not adopted on the record's word.** On `origin/main`, `SaveMetaItemRequestSchema.packageId`'s description (`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`) still says a `draft` save naming no package writes "the env-local draft" when the item's active row is not package-bound. This PR changes exactly that arm: one package's draft is inherited, and two or more are refused `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`. PR #23654 rewrote the publish and discard descriptions for the same rule, so the three doors' published texts now disagree. Finding ①7 stands. The runtime change is accepted as the record judges it.

**The seat's ruling (the PR #23654 precedent):**
1. **The published description.** Rewrite `SaveMetaItemRequestSchema.packageId`'s draft arm to state the rule this PR ships, in the same words the publish and discard descriptions use for it. Regenerate with the spec generators (`gen:schema`, `gen:docs`, and whatever `check:generated` names). ⛔ Never hand-edit a generated file. Add `'@objectstack/spec': patch` to the changeset. The `packages/spec` hunk is cross-lane `domain:spec`; this seat declares it on #18883.
2. **`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`.** The claim 6196478876 is amended to say so; the PR body and the changeset follow. Three reasons: the published description changes with the narrowing; the two-package arm narrows; and a permission-set body naming package Q, saved naming no package, is now accepted where it was refused 400 (ADR-0086 D3), which widens. Declaring `yes` is never wrong (`references/lanes/spec.md`). PR #23654 is the precedent.
3. **Name every derived change in the changeset, FROM → TO.** These are the two the record found unnamed:
   - `If-None-Match: *` on such a save now answers `409 METADATA_CONFLICT`;
   - the permission-set body naming Q is now accepted.
   - The `If-Match` with Q's token, now accepted, belongs there too.
4. **OQ3, measure-first, not fixed here.** Over `[package-unbound, Q]` drafts with no active binding, measure whether the strict draft read serves its content from a different row than its version. Report the reading. If it diverges, this seat files the card. ⛔ Do not widen this PR to fix it.
